before: C# 14 field-backed properties can use field inside an accessor to refer to compiler-generated backing storage. get; returns that same storage.
In set, value is the incoming assignment. The if statement rejects a negative value before the later field = value statement can store it.
After Minutes has been set to 5, assigning -1 throws before field is changed. The property still contains 5. This example explicitly targets C# 14 on .NET 10, not a preview compiler.
Expected behavior from this example: Rejected, then 5 on separate lines. This expected result is a reasoned prediction until a compiler test is recorded.

Optional local transfer: Add an upper bound of 180. Check zero, 180 and 181, and verify a rejected assignment preserves the previous value. This is a separate local practice task, not a requirement to mark the reading complete.
after: In C# 14, field inside a property accessor refers to storage created by the compiler. The short get; reads that same stored value.
A setter runs when code assigns the property. Inside set, value is the new value being offered.
This setter checks for a negative number before reaching field = value. A negative number throws an error, so the assignment to storage is skipped.
The program prints Rejected, then 5. Setting Minutes to 5 succeeds. Setting it to -1 throws before changing the stored number.
Validation happens before the write, so a rejected value leaves the last accepted value in place. A nonnegative value reaches field = value and replaces the stored number.
